newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-Danish long yields up to 7.07 pct in year.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Danish long yields up to 7.07 pct in year.

text.p: Danish bond yields will climb modestly over the next 12 months, a Reuter consensus poll of 17 economists indicated on Thursday.
An average of forecasts showed the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006, currently yielding around 6.59 percent, up at 7.07 percent in 12 months' time at end-March 1998.
By end June 1997, the benchmark was seen yielding 6.67 percent, rising to an average 6.91 percent by end-September.

The 10-year yield gap with Germany was expected to be 71 basis points at end-June, unchanged from Thursday, widening a little to an average 76 basis points at end-September, before slipping back minimally to 75 at end-March 1998, the poll showed.

Three-month money rates were seen at 3.74 percent in three months' time, 3.90 percent in six months and 4.27 percent in a year's time, compared to the present approximate 3.65 percent, the poll said. --Eva Elgaard Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 96 96 58
